audience.text: Python developers and researchers who need to process TeX/LaTeX documents programmatically without installing system-wide TeX engines.

capabilities.text: The library parses real TeX/LaTeX source through its own interpreter, handling tokenizer, macro expansion, and mode-machine dispatch for control sequences, groups, and paragraph text.
capabilities.title: Parse and interpret TeX/LaTeX source

capabilities.text: Output devices `PdfDevice`, `DviDevice`, and `SvgDevice` produce finished pages; `SvgDevice` embeds glyph outlines directly as `<path>` elements.
capabilities.title: Generate PDF, DVI, and SVG output

capabilities.text: Font metrics and glyph outlines are resolved from bundled `.tfm` and `.pfb` files, independent of the target output format.
capabilities.title: Resolve bundled Computer Modern fonts

capabilities.text: Job behavior is configured via `TeXOptions`, supporting `job_name`, `magnification`, `extra_font_paths`, `extra_format_paths`, and format loading.
capabilities.title: Configure job options

capabilities.text: Input sources are created from `Path`, `str`, or `bytes` using `create_input_source`, supporting both file and string inputs.
capabilities.title: Handle input sources flexibly

capabilities.text: Exceptions `AsposeTeXError`, `InputError`, `EngineError`, and `FontError` enable targeted error handling for different failure modes.
capabilities.title: Provide structured exception handling

limitations.text: Pre-Alpha release: core engine and public API are under active development, and interfaces may change between releases.
Default `load_format='plain'` does not fully load Knuth's Plain TeX macro cascade; examples use `load_format=False` for runnable documents.
Math-mode content (`$...$`, `$$...$$`) is parsed but not laid out; no math atoms, fractions, or radicals reach the page.
Table alignment (`halign`, `valign`) is registered but not implemented and raises `NotImplementedError`.
Automatic hyphenation is inactive: `patterns` and `hyphenation` are parsed and discarded, and the bundled hyphenation directory is empty.
Named file-stream I/O (`openin`, `openout`, `closein`, `closeout`, `read`) raises `NotImplementedError`; only `write 16`, `write -1`, `message`, and `errmessage` are implemented.

problems_solved.text: Enables TeX/LaTeX processing in pure Python without external dependencies like MiKTeX or TeX Live.
Provides bundled Computer Modern fonts and metrics, allowing output generation without external font files.
Supports in-memory and file-based output for PDF, DVI, and SVG formats through a unified API.

product_summary.text: Aspose.TeX FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, pure-Python library for TeX/LaTeX processing that parses real source and produces PDF, DVI, or SVG output without requiring an external TeX installation.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported TeX primitives beyond those explicitly documented is not fully specified.
Whether future releases will support full Plain TeX macro loading without requiring `load_format=False` is unclear.
The behavior of `TeXOptions.extra_format_paths` relative to working directory precedence is described but not exhaustively tested.
The completeness of the bundled Computer Modern font set (e.g., all variants and encodings) is not detailed.
The scope of `TeXJob.messages`—whether it includes all possible diagnostic types—is not fully enumerated.
The threading or concurrency safety of `TeXJob` instances is not stated.
The long-term support plan for this FOSS release versus the Enterprise Edition is not detailed.
Whether additional output formats beyond PDF, DVI, and SVG are planned is not indicated.

workflows.name: Create and run a TeX job
workflows.text: Create an input source using `create_input_source`, configure options with `TeXOptions`, instantiate `TeXJob` with a device (`PdfDevice`, `DviDevice`, or `SvgDevice`), and call `run()` to generate output.

workflows.name: Collect run diagnostics
workflows.text: Access `TeXJob.messages` after running to retrieve diagnostic messages, and configure Python logging for engine output.

workflows.name: Write output to file or memory
workflows.text: Pass a `Path` to output devices to write directly to disk, or leave it empty to retrieve `bytes` from `get_bytes()` or `get_all_pages()`.
